model_answer:
Let $\dfrac x1=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z-2}{3}=\lambda$; the general point on the line is $Q(\lambda,\ 1+2\lambda,\ 2+3\lambda)$ [1]
Direction ratios of $PQ$: $\lambda-1,\ 2\lambda-5,\ 3\lambda-1$ [1]
$PQ\perp$ line: $1(\lambda-1)+2(2\lambda-5)+3(3\lambda-1)=0\Rightarrow14\lambda=14\Rightarrow\lambda=1$ [1]
Foot of the perpendicular $Q(1,3,5)$; length $PQ=\sqrt{0+9+4}=\sqrt{13}$ units [1]
$Q$ is the mid-point of $PP'$, so the image is $P'=2Q-P=(1,0,7)$ [1]

parts.stem: Write the direction ratios of $L_1$ and of $L_2$.
Find the cosine of the angle between the two paths.

Find the shortest distance between the two paths.
**OR** Find the point where the path $L_1$ meets the $xy$-plane.
parts.model_answer:
$\vec a_2-\vec a_1=\hat i-3\hat j-2\hat k$; $\vec b_1\times\vec b_2=-3\hat i+3\hat k$, with magnitude $3\sqrt2$ [1]
$d=\left|\dfrac{(1)(-3)+(-3)(0)+(-2)(3)}{3\sqrt2}\right|=\dfrac{9}{3\sqrt2}=\dfrac{3\sqrt2}{2}$ km [1]
**OR:** a general point of $L_1$ is $(1+\lambda,\ 2-\lambda,\ 1+\lambda)$; on the $xy$-plane $z=0$, so $\lambda=-1$ [1]; the point is $(0,3,0)$ [1].
